content.text: You’ve made it to the end of all the chapters – I hope you’re proud of all the work you’ve put in! Don’t worry if you found some things hard: topics such as closures and optionals *are* hard, so if they took some time to learn that’s just a sign your brain is working properly.

Now, the question is: where can you go next? Well, you have two options. The first is to continue with all the practice activities you've unlocked and take your daily challenges – this will help you solidify all the things you've learned so far.
The second is to check out the range of books I've written that I hope will help you answer that question:

bullets: If you’d like to start using Swift to make iOS apps, you should read Hacking with Swift. It’s available free online [here](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/read) but you can buy the premium edition with bonus content [here](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/hacking-with-swift).

If you’d like to improve your knowledge of the Swift language, tackling more advanced features such as generics, custom operators, and functional programming, you should read Pro Swift. It’s available to buy [here](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/pro-swift).

If you’d like to learn to make games using Swift, you’re ready for my book Dive Into SpriteKit – you get to choose how each game project should develop. It’s available to buy [here](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/dive-into-spritekit).

If you’d like to try other Apple platforms, I have books teaching [macOS](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/hacking-with-macos), [watchOS](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/hacking-with-watchos), and [tvOS](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/store/hacking-with-tvos).

content.text: Congratulations on finishing this course – I hope you learned a lot, and that you’re able to have a lot of fun with your new coding skills!
Now, are you ready for one last test of your skills…?

title: Where now?
postscript: You can go back and re-read any of these chapters whenever you want – keep your Swift skills fresh!
question: Which of these statements are true?
hint: These questions are taken from a variety of chapters – you might need to re-read one of them if you're not sure about an answer.

correct.answer: Closures can capture values around them.
Structs are copied differently from classes.
Variadic functions take any number of parameters.
Throwing functions must be called using `try`.

wrong.answer: Functions inside structs are called closures.
Swift automatically generates the shorthand parameter names `#0`, `#1`, and so on.
Classes may not contain private methods.
wrong.reason: Classes are perfectly able to contain private methods.

wrong.answer: You can make a new struct by inheriting from any other structs that are not declared using `final`.
Extensions can only be used on protocols.
wrong.reason: You can also extend specific types.
Implicitly unwrapped optionals such as `String!` might be nil.
